raw_case_text:
We report the case of a 44-year-old multiparous woman, without previous medical history, having a positive family history for breast cancer in her paternal aunt. She presented elsewhere for a one-month history of cough and abdominal distention, followed by episodes of fever at 39 C. Abdominal ultrasound was done, showing large ascites and a right ovarian mass.
An abdominopelvic MRI was done showing a hyperintense, heterogeneous mass of the right ovary, measuring 20 x 17 mm, with restriction of diffusion, in favor of a malignant process.
Tumor markers showed an elevated CA 125 level of 543 and normal CA 19-9 level of 13.2. Serum C-reactive protein (CRP) was 53.
A diagnostic abdominal tap was done with cytology examination showing no malignant cells in the peritoneal fluid.
A PET/CT scan was also done revealing peritoneal thickening and diffuse peritoneal fixation with hypermetabolism at the right ovary (SUV = 6.7) of 2 cm, as well as bilateral pleural fluid that was not hypermetabolic.
The patient was admitted at our department for further investigations. New work-up with total body CT scan was done showing moderate enhanced ascites associated with mesenteric fat streaking with millimetric nodules suggestive of peritoneal carcinomatosis (Figure 1).
Abdominal tap was repeated revealing only inflammatory reaction and serous fluid without evidence of malignant cells and with negative culture. An ultrasound-guided Tru-cut biopsy of the peritoneum was performed and revealed only inflammatory changes without malignant cells. Right pleural fluid was aspirated and sent for cytology and culture. Analysis showed no evidence of bacteria, infection, or malignant cells.
Ultimately, a laparoscopic exploration was done with multiple biopsies taken from peritoneal nodules. Histological result showed a necrotizing, epithelioid, and gigantocellular granulomatous reaction, with Ziehl staining showing exceptional acido-alcohol resistant bacilli compatible with Koch bacilli (Figure 2). Subsequently, pulmonary sampling was done and samples were analyzed for Mycobacterium tuberculosis by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), with a negative result showing no sign of pulmonary infection.
The patient was started on quadritherapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide) for 2 months with significant improvement in her clinical picture and weight gain of 4 kg and will continue for an additional 6 months of biotherapy with rifampicin and isoniazid. Follow-up imaging with abdominal MRI was done showing no ascites or masses in the abdomen.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 44-year-old female presented with a 1-month history of cough, progressive abdominal distention, and episodic high-grade fevers.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 1-month history of dry cough and abdominal distention, subsequently accompanied by spiking fevers up to 39 °C.
subjective.past_medical_history: Multiparous without prior medical illness. Family history notable for breast cancer in a paternal aunt.
subjective.review_of_systems: Complained of cough, abdominal distention, and high-grade fevers. Home medications and allergies: unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: Body temperature 39 °C, notable for abdominal distention with clinically detectable ascites.
objective.routine_investigations: Serum C-reactive protein (CRP): 53 mg/L. Tumor markers: CA 125 elevated at 543 U/mL, CA 19-9 normal at 13.2 U/mL. Repeat diagnostic paracentesis: serous fluid with nonspecific inflammatory reaction, negative bacterial culture, and absence of malignant cells on cytology. Diagnostic thoracentesis (right pleural fluid): negative for bacterial growth, acute infection, or malignant cells.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominopelvic ultrasound: large-volume ascites and a right ovarian mass. Abdominopelvic MRI: heterogeneous hyperintense right ovarian mass measuring 20 x 17 mm with diffusion restriction. Whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT: diffuse peritoneal thickening and hypermetabolic fixation, hypermetabolic right ovarian lesion (SUV max 6.7, 2 cm), and bilateral non-hypermetabolic pleural effusions. Total body CT scan: moderate ascites, mesenteric fat stranding, and millimetric peritoneal nodules mimicking carcinomatosis. Ultrasound-guided Tru-cut peritoneal biopsy: demonstrated inflammatory changes without malignant cells. Diagnostic laparoscopy: multiple biopsies from peritoneal nodules demonstrated necrotizing epithelioid and gigantocellular granulomatous inflammation.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Peritoneal and ovarian tuberculosis mimicking advanced ovarian carcinomatosis. Histopathology of laparoscopic peritoneal nodule biopsies revealed necrotizing epithelioid and gigantocellular granulomas, and Ziehl-Neelsen staining demonstrated acid-fast bacilli compatible with Mycobacterium tuberculosis; pulmonary PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis was negative, confirming isolated peritoneal involvement. Ovarian cancer and peritoneal carcinomatosis were ruled out.
Treatment & Outcome: Treated with four-drug antitubercular quadritherapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide) for 2 months, followed by biotherapy (rifampicin and isoniazid) for 6 months. Showed marked clinical improvement with 4-kg weight gain; follow-up abdominal MRI revealed complete resolution of ascites and ovarian masses.
